name: Glacier
lede: Glacier is a dark, greyish blue-violet that appears in Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary, whose origin the sources do not explain.

sections.title: A name from ice
sections.body:
Our only record of the name as a color is Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary, plate 39 [1]. The swatch reads as a greyish purplish blue in ISCC-NBS terms [1], much darker than ice looks in sunlight. Garfield, counting the sources of color names, lists glacier blue among 121 names taken from geographical elements [2].

That is all the books give. They mention glaciers as places, as the source of meltwater that greens the Himalayan valleys [3], and as the blue-drawn glaciers on the white of snow on maps [4]. None of them says what glacier-the-color was supposed to look like. Close relatives in the graph include [[steel-blue]], [[slate-grey]], [[navy]] and [[indigo]].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: The color is present in 275 of 23,781 archive paintings and plays a hidden color in 52 percent of the 139 where our within-painting lens finds it [5]. Henri Matisse is its most devoted painter, in 4 of 50 works, 4.5 times the baseline [5]. The earliest match is 1301, which is 629 years before the name's first record in our sources, 1930 [5]. As photographed, a match is a look-alike hue, not evidence about pigments or glaciers.
